findings.source_passage: the first whale attacked by our brotherhood was not killed with any sordid intent. Those were the knightly days of our profession, when we only bore arms to succor the distressed, and not to fill men's lamp-feeders.
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'Those were the knightly days of our profession' is a register-defining, ironically elevated declaration that establishes the mock-heroic tone of the whole chapter; the draft collapses it into a single clause, losing the rhetorical cadence and the 'knightly days' formulation.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Those were the knightly days of our profession, when we only bore arms to succor the distressed, and not to fill men's lamp-feeders' as close to verbatim as compression allows.

findings.source_passage: it was an admirable artistic exploit, rarely achieved by the best harpooneers of the present day; inasmuch as this Leviathan was slain at the very first dart.
findings.source_locator: paragraph 3, after Perseus kills the monster
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'admirable artistic exploit, rarely achieved by the best harpooneers of the present day' is a signature comic-ironic aside that applies professional harpoon standards to myth; the draft reduces it to 'slain, too, at the very first dart,' losing the self-congratulatory harpooneer's-eye evaluative voice entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'It was an admirable artistic exploit, rarely achieved by the best harpooneers of the present day' before noting the first-dart kill.

findings.source_passage: placed before the strict and piercing truth, this whole story will fare like that fish, flesh, and fowl idol of the Philistines, Dagon by name; who being planted before the ark of Israel, his horse's head and both the palms of his hands fell off from him
findings.why_it_matters: The Dagon passage is preserved nearly verbatim in the draft, which is good; however, the setup clause 'placed before the strict and piercing truth' is present, so this is largely intact. Minor point only.
findings.suggested_fix: No action needed here; passage is adequately preserved.

findings.source_passage: that antique Crockett and Kit Carson—that brawny doer of rejoicing good deeds
findings.why_it_matters: This is preserved verbatim in the draft, so no loss. Noted for completeness.

findings.source_passage: Vishnoo, who, by the first of his ten earthly incarnations, has for ever set apart and sanctified the whale.
findings.why_it_matters: The clause 'has for ever set apart and sanctified the whale' carries significant interpretive weight—it is the theological culmination of the chapter's argument, elevating whaling to a divine, sanctified vocation. Its absence removes the chapter's highest rhetorical claim.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Vishnoo, who, by the first of his ten earthly incarnations, has for ever set apart and sanctified the whale' after introducing Vishnoo.

summary: The draft is broadly faithful with no high-severity signature losses; three medium findings—loss of 'the knightly days of our profession,' loss of 'admirable artistic exploit,' and loss of the 'for ever set apart and sanctified the whale' clause—represent voice flattening and one interpretive thinning that fall just below the regenerate threshold, but a revision pass to restore those three passages is strongly recommended.
